> **Paths in this skill.** `<plugin-root>` is this plugin's own folder, the folder two levels above the folder this SKILL.md sits in. In Claude Code it is also `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. `<merlin-data>` is your business folder, `${user_config.data_dir}`; where that is empty or still reads as written, use the `data_root` value in `~/.merlin/instance.json`. `<about-me>` is your about-me folder, `<memory>` your company memory folder, `<task-list>` your task list file, `<merlin-manifest>` Merlin's manifest file and `<run-state>` the folder for run state. Each is the path the start-up status line names, inside the HQ folder it names (or the path Merlin's setup script prints, run as `setup.sh --where`, under about_me, memory, task_list, manifest or run_state). Never build one of these from the business folder by hand. Write each of these as an absolute path in every command you run, because a shell cannot expand any of them.

# Merlin home

The Merlin home is a page on this computer that shows what Merlin has stored for your
business folder: your projects, each project's notes and files, your about-me files, your
skills and plugins. It only shows. Nothing is made or changed from it except its two
settings (menu position and light or dark).

A small home server on this computer serves the page. It listens on this computer only,
stops by itself after 8 hours with no use, and never writes in your business folder.

The one script is `<plugin-root>/hooks/home_context.py`, written `<home>` below. Run it
with `python3 -I -B`. In every command, `<folder>` is the folder this chat is open on, as a
full path.

## Open the home

Said as: "open my Merlin home", "show my dashboard", "show my Merlin home".

1. Run `python3 -I -B "<home>" address "<folder>"`. It makes sure the home server runs and
   prints one line: the address to open. It works when the home is switched off too.
2. Show the browser pane beside the chat (the show-pane tool with pane "preview"; load the
   tool first if it is only listed), then open that address in it.
3. Say in one line that the home is open. Never say it is open unless a browser pane tool
   opened it in this chat.

If this chat has no browser pane tools (a terminal, a scheduled run), say so in one line
and give the address, so the person can open it in a chat that has the pane. Never open the
home in another browser or another app.

If the command exits with an error, say: "I could not open your Merlin home on this
computer," then the reason it printed, in plain words. Do not try another way.

## Turn it off or back on

Said as: "turn off the Merlin home", "stop opening the Merlin home", "turn the Merlin home
back on".

- Off: run `python3 -I -B "<home>" off "<folder>"`. From the next new chat the home no
  longer opens by itself. It still opens when asked for.
- On: run `python3 -I -B "<home>" on "<folder>"`. The next new chat opens it again.

Each prints one line. Tell the person in one line what changed and how to undo it, from that
line. The switch is one empty file, `home/off` in Merlin's run-state folder; these two
commands are the only ones that write it.

## Boundaries

- This skill opens the home, or turns it off or on. It never creates, edits or deletes
  anything else, in the business folder or anywhere.
- A request for one construction project's dashboard belongs to the construction add-on, not
  here. A marketing or social media dashboard is not the Merlin home either.
- To stop the home server now (it starts again with the next new chat), run
  `python3 -I -B "<home>" stop`.
